articles.title: TikTok accused of becoming a gateway to the online sex industry for young girls
articles.summary: TikTok is facing scrutiny over allegations that its platform is being used to draw young women and teenage girls towards the online sex industry, with
articles.body: TikTok is facing scrutiny over allegations that its platform is being used to draw young women and teenage girls towards the online sex industry, with performers on OnlyFans allegedly using seemingly harmless lifestyle videos to promote their paid adult content elsewhere.A study by UK-based Centre to End All Sexual Exploitation (Cease) and Australian campaign group Collective Shout has found that some of OnlyFans' most popular young female creators use coded language, emojis and suggestive gestures in TikTok videos to direct viewers towards their sexually explicit content on other platforms.The findings, reported by The Guardian, are based on a year-long examination of non-explicit TikTok posts by popular OnlyFans performers. Researchers also followed recommendations generated by TikTok's algorithm to understand how such content was being circulated.Although TikTok does not allow users to promote OnlyFans directly or share links to the platform, the study found that creators had developed ways to get around these restrictions. They allegedly use everyday videos featuring shopping trips, pets, baking, skincare and makeup routines to hint at the availability of adult content for sale elsewhere.Some performers use the word "corn" instead of "porn", while others place a corn emoji alongside a star emoji to avoid triggering content moderation systems. The report also highlights the use of seemingly innocent 'get ready with me' videos, commonly known as GRWM, to make indirect references to pornography.The researchers described this as a "TikTok to OnlyFans pipeline", arguing that the platform is helping adult content creators reach a much wider audience, including teenagers.The study also found that several viral videos presented selling sexual content on OnlyFans as a route to wealth, financial independence and a luxurious lifestyle."The one of the most pervasive messages across these posts is that selling sexual services on OnlyFans gives you a fabulous life – a life filled with freedom, fun, friendship and lots of money," the report stated.Some videos featured images of cash, luxury homes, private jets and expensive cars, accompanied by captions suggesting that young women could achieve financial success by selling adult content.Other posts portrayed OnlyFans as a way out of poverty and unemployment. According to the researchers, performers often shared stories of how joining the platform had transformed their lives and helped them support their families.Opening an account was presented as a way of escaping difficult financial circumstances and acquiring expensive possessions that women and their families could not otherwise afford.However, the report cautioned against assuming that such earnings were typical. While OnlyFans data shows that its top 5,000 creators have earned more than $1 million each since the platform was launched in 2016, the average annual earnings of its estimated five million creators are believed to be around $1,000.Melinda Tankard Reist of Collective Shout criticised TikTok for allowing such promotional content to circulate.“an industrial-scale digital pimp funnelling girls into the sex industry”, she said, describing the platform's role.She added, “It is our view that young women and girls deserve to be protected from a predatory industry grooming them to be producers of explicit content.”Tankard Reist said the research was commissioned amid concerns that popular OnlyFans performers, including Sophie Rain and Ari Kytsya, had built large TikTok followings among teenage girls while promoting the financial benefits of producing pornography.Rain gained prominence through videos filmed at the Bop House, a luxury pornography production house in Miami. The property is home to a rotating group of women who create and sell sexual content on OnlyFans. Videos announcing auditions for new members are also shared on TikTok, where aspiring recruits post suggestive dance videos and tag the Bop House.The report further highlighted how OnlyFans performers use their social media popularity to secure mainstream brand partnerships. Their TikTok content can include promotions for everyday products such as pet food, burgers and pineapple juice, alongside advertisements for sex toys and condoms.Kytsya, who describes herself as a “mattress actress”, was appointed a brand ambassador for Urban Decay, a cosmetics brand owned by L'Oréal and popular among teenagers. In advertisements that attracted millions of views on TikTok, she promoted makeup products using references to their performance on mattresses.The researchers have called for existing restrictions on showing pornography to people under 18 to be extended to content that promotes or is associated with the sex industry.Responding to the findings, a TikTok spokesperson said, “TikTok strictly prohibits the sharing or showing of sexual content and we use advanced technologies to enforce our community guidelines. In addition, our systems are designed to prevent age-inappropriate content from reaching teens.”An OnlyFans spokesperson said, “OnlyFans is a platform for people aged 18 and over and we have strict onboarding processes to prevent minors accessing the platform.”You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Need to suffer consequences’: New York woman slams judge over 8.5-year sentence for man who stabbed her 22 times
articles.summary: A 23-year-old woman in New York has criticised a Bronx judge for giving the man who stabbed her 22 times an eight-and-a-half-year prison sentence, saying
articles.body: A 23-year-old woman in New York has criticised a Bronx judge for giving the man who stabbed her 22 times an eight-and-a-half-year prison sentence, saying the punishment does not reflect the severity of the attack or its lasting impact on her life.Kaitlynn Berman spoke to the New York Post on Friday, two days after Joseph, the man who attacked her in March 2025, was sentenced to eight-and-a-half years in state prison, followed by five years of post-release supervision.“He stabbed me more times than the years he was sentenced for,” Berman told the newspaper.She also objected to the suggestion that her attacker was young enough to turn his life around, saying the focus should instead be on the consequences of his actions.Survivor says sentence was too lightBerman said she believed Joseph had received a lenient sentence and that the physical and psychological effects of the attack continued to affect her.“I think it was a very, very light sentence,” she said. “He needs more than eight and a half years, and people really need to know who he is.”She added: “People need to know that he’s a monster.”Berman said she had suffered daily trauma since the attack and would have to live with its effects long after Joseph's release.The New York Post reported that Berman vomited after learning about the sentence, which she described as "very light".Judge acknowledges impact of attackDuring the sentencing, Bronx Judge Lewis addressed Joseph, telling him that the attack had affected Berman's life and urging him to reflect on his actions.“I hope you hear what I’m saying. I hope you think about what you’ve done. I’m sure you have. I’m sure you’ve had many sleepless nights. But you’ll never be able to take away what you did to Ms. Berman and how you affected her life,” the judge said.He then said the sentence had been agreed upon and imposed the punishment as promised.Lewis was appointed to the bench by New York Governor Kathy Hochul in 2023.Berman, however, rejected the argument that her attacker deserved an opportunity to change his life, saying the consequences of the crime should take precedence.“They said that he’s still young and has time to change his life around,” she told the newspaper.“I think it doesn’t matter if you have time to change your life around. I think it matters of what you already did. You need to suffer the consequences.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: ‘My family, I face threat’: Italy minister says his private data leaked on dark web
articles.summary: Italian foreign minister Antonio Tajani has said cybercriminals are circulating his personal information on the dark web, exposing him and his family to
articles.body: Italian foreign minister Antonio Tajani has said cybercriminals are circulating his personal information on the dark web, exposing him and his family to threats and intimidation.Tajani revealed the breach in a social media post on Saturday, but did not disclose what information had been leaked or identify those behind the operation. He indicated that the activity was continuing, with criminals also trying to obtain more details about him and his relatives.“For days, cybercriminals have been spreading my personal data on the dark web and seeking other information, in fact exposing me and my family to new threats and intimidation,” Tajani said, adding that the criminals "are prepared to pay for other details on me and my loved ones.”Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni has blamed "pro-Russian hackers" for the leak.Meloni, in a separate statement, also expressed solidarity with Tajani “following the revelations about the activities of pro-Russian hackers, and the publication on the dark web of personal data."She called attempts to sell confidential information about government officials “a matter of grave concern that must be addressed with the utmost determination.”The dark web is a part of the internet that is not accessible through ordinary search engines and requires specialised software to access. It is sometimes used to trade stolen personal information and other illicit material.The disclosure comes amid a series of security incidents across Europe. Hoax bomb threats have led to flight diversions and security concerns at broadcasters. There have also been recent attacks on supermarket refrigeration systems and incursions by drones.Tajani, who also serves as one of Italy's deputy prime ministers, said he would not be deterred by the threats and vowed to strengthen security cooperation.“I will not allow myself to be intimidated in any way,” Tajani said. “I will continue working to defend my ministry, and Italy, and I will further strengthen the ties and cooperation to protect ourselves together.”He did not link the alleged cyberattack to any particular group or country. However, he reiterated the Italian government's support for Ukraine.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Florida governor Ron DeSantis denies plans for 2028 presidential run, calls report ‘fabricated’
articles.summary: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis reacts to a Washington Post report claiming he is preparing for a 2028 presidential run, calling it fabricated. He asserts he hasn't contacted anyone about a potential campaign, labeling it a clickbait attempt.
articles.body: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis has pushed back against a report that he is preparing to seek the Republican nomination for president in 2028, accusing The Washington Post of inventing claims about his political plans.The newspaper reported on Friday, citing three people briefed on the matter, that DeSantis was making preparations for another White House campaign. The governor rejected the account in a post on X, saying he had not contacted anyone about a possible run.“The Washington Post is fabricating this out of whole cloth. I have not reached out to anybody about running for anything. Just another pathetic attempt to garner clicks. Using anonymous sources of course!” DeSantis wrote.The report emerged days after Democrats made significant gains in the November 3 midterm elections, winning control of Congress. Florida, however, remained a Republican stronghold, with the party retaining the governor's office.Republican Byron Donalds defeated Democrat David Jolly in the Florida gubernatorial race, becoming the state's first Black governor. Donalds, who had Trump's backing, campaigned on affordability and pledged to continue the conservative policies pursued by DeSantis. He also benefited from a substantial campaign fund.Donalds has represented Florida in the US House of Representatives since 2021 and previously served two terms in the state legislature. He will succeed DeSantis as governor.According to The Washington Post, the state's election results have strengthened DeSantis' position within the Republican Party as attention begins to shift towards the 2028 presidential contest.Dan Eberhart, a longtime GOP donor who worked on DeSantis' 2024 campaign, told the newspaper that Florida's performance had given the governor greater standing among potential candidates.“Florida’s walls not being breached by the blue wave gives DeSantis more credibility than nearly anyone in the opening days of the 2028 primary,” Eberhart said.DeSantis, 48, previously sought the Republican presidential nomination in 2024 but failed to overcome Donald Trump's support among party voters. articles.title: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan have pledged to donate 99% of their Meta shares; here's the open letter they wrote to their eldest daughter Maxima in 2015; it makes a promises that ...
articles.summary: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan made a promise to their eldest daughter, Maxima in 2015.
articles.body: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan made a promise to their eldest daughter, Maxima in 2015. The two said that they will donate 99% of their Meta (then Facebook) shares, but it was about more than giving away their wealth. In an open letter written after her birth, the couple pledged to donate their Facebook shares, then valued at around $45 billion, to help build a better world for the next generation. They also outlined a future focused on curing diseases, improving education, expanding internet access and promoting equality. More than a decade later, the letter offers a glimpse into the ambitions that shaped their philanthropic mission and the promises they made to their daughter.Here's the open letter Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan wrote in 2015A letter to our daughterDear Max,Your mother and I don't yet have the words to describe the hope you give us for the future. Your new life is full of promise, and we hope you will be happy and healthy so you can explore it fully. You've already given us a reason to reflect on the world we hope you live in.Like all parents, we want you to grow up in a world better than ours today.While headlines often focus on what's wrong, in many ways the world is getting better. Health is improving. Poverty is shrinking. Knowledge is growing. People are connecting. Technological progress in every field means your life should be dramatically better than ours today.We will do our part to make this happen, not only because we love you, but also because we have a moral responsibility to all children in the next generation.We believe all lives have equal value, and that includes the many more people who will live in future generations than live today. Our society has an obligation to invest now to improve the lives of all those coming into this world, not just those already here.But right now, we don't always collectively direct our resources at the biggest opportunities and problems your generation will face.Consider disease. Today we spend about 50 times more as a society treating people who are sick than we invest in research so you won't get sick in the first place.Medicine has only been a real science for less than 100 years, and we've already seen complete cures for some diseases and good progress for others. As technology accelerates, we have a real shot at preventing, curing or managing all or most of the rest in the next 100 years.Today, most people die from five things -- heart disease, cancer, stroke, neurodegenerative and infectious diseases -- and we can make faster progress on these and other problems.Once we recognize that your generation and your children's generation may not have to suffer from disease, we collectively have a responsibility to tilt our investments a bit more towards the future to make this reality. Your mother and I want to do our part.Curing disease will take time. Over short periods of five or ten years, it may not seem like we're making much of a difference. But over the long term, seeds planted now will grow, and one day, you or your children will see what we can only imagine: a world without suffering from disease.There are so many opportunities just like this. If society focuses more of its energy on these great challenges, we will leave your generation a much better world.• • •Our hopes for your generation focus on two ideas: advancing human potential and promoting equality.Advancing human potential is about pushing the boundaries on how great a human life can be.Can you learn and experience 100 times more than we do today?Can our generation cure disease so you live much longer and healthier lives?Can we connect the world so you have access to every idea, person and opportunity?Can we harness more clean energy so you can invent things we can't conceive of today while protecting the environment?Can we cultivate entrepreneurship so you can build any business and solve any challenge to grow peace and prosperity?Promoting equality is about making sure everyone has access to these opportunities -- regardless of the nation, families or circumstances they are born into.Our society must do this not only for justice or charity, but for the greatness of human progress.Today we are robbed of the potential so many have to offer. The only way to achieve our full potential is to channel the talents, ideas and contributions of every person in the world.Can our generation eliminate poverty and hunger?Can we provide everyone with basic healthcare?Can we build inclusive and welcoming communities?Can we nurture peaceful and understanding relationships between people of all nations?Can we truly empower everyone -- women, children, underrepresented minorities, immigrants and the unconnected?If our generation makes the right investments, the answer to each of these questions can be yes -- and hopefully within your lifetime.• • •This mission -- advancing human potential and promoting equality -- will require a new approach for all working towards these goals.We must make long term investments over 25, 50 or even 100 years. The greatest challenges require very long time horizons and cannot be solved by short term thinking.We must engage directly with the people we serve. We can't empower people if we don't understand the needs and desires of their communities.We must build technology to make change. Many institutions invest money in these challenges, but most progress comes from productivity gains through innovation.We must participate in policy and advocacy to shape debates. Many institutions are unwilling to do this, but progress must be supported by movements to be sustainable.We must back the strongest and most independent leaders in each field. Partnering with experts is more effective for the mission than trying to lead efforts ourselves.We must take risks today to learn lessons for tomorrow. We're early in our learning and many things we try won't work, but we'll listen and learn and keep improving.• • •Our experience with personalized learning, internet access, and community education and health has shaped our philosophy.Our generation grew up in classrooms where we all learned the same things at the same pace regardless of our interests or needs.Your generation will set goals for what you want to become -- like an engineer, health worker, writer or community leader. You'll have technology that understands how you learn best and where you need to focus. You'll advance quickly in subjects that interest you most, and get as much help as you need in your most challenging areas. You'll explore topics that aren't even offered in schools today. Your teachers will also have better tools and data to help you achieve your goals.Even better, students around the world will be able to use personalized learning tools over the internet, even if they don't live near good schools. Of course it will take more than technology to give everyone a fair start in life, but personalized learning can be one scalable way to give all children a better education and more equal opportunity.We're starting to build this technology now, and the results are already promising. Not only do students perform better on tests, but they gain the skills and confidence to learn anything they want. And this journey is just beginning. The technology and teaching will rapidly improve every year you're in school.Your mother and I have both taught students and we've seen what it takes to make this work. It will take working with the strongest leaders in education to help schools around the world adopt personalized learning. It will take engaging with communities, which is why we're starting in our San Francisco Bay Area community. It will take building new technology and trying new ideas. And it will take making mistakes and learning many lessons before achieving these goals.But once we understand the world we can create for your generation, we have a responsibility as a society to focus our investments on the future to make this reality.Together, we can do this. And when we do, personalized learning will not only help students in good schools, it will help provide more equal opportunity to anyone with an internet connection.• • •Many of the greatest opportunities for your generation will come from giving everyone access to the internet.People often think of the internet as just for entertainment or communication. But for the majority of people in the world, the internet can be a lifeline.It provides education if you don't live near a good school. It provides health information on how to avoid diseases or raise healthy children if you don't live near a doctor. It provides financial services if you don't live near a bank. It provides access to jobs and opportunities if you don't live in a good economy.The internet is so important that for every 10 people who gain internet access, about one person is lifted out of poverty and about one new job is created.Yet still more than half of the world's population -- more than 4 billion people -- don't have access to the internet.If our generation connects them, we can lift hundreds of millions of people out of poverty. We can also help hundreds of millions of children get an education and save millions of lives by helping people avoid disease.This is another long term effort that can be advanced by technology and partnership. It will take inventing new technology to make the internet more affordable and bring access to unconnected areas. It will take partnering with governments, non-profits and companies. It will take engaging with communities to understand what they need. Good people will have different views on the best path forward, and we will try many efforts before we succeed.But together we can succeed and create a more equal world.• • •Technology can't solve problems by itself. Building a better world starts with building strong and healthy communities.Children have the best opportunities when they can learn. And they learn best when they're healthy.Health starts early -- with loving family, good nutrition and a safe, stable environment.Children who face traumatic experiences early in life often develop less healthy minds and bodies. Studies show physical changes in brain development leading to lower cognitive ability.Your mother is a doctor and educator, and she has seen this firsthand.If you have an unhealthy childhood, it's difficult to reach your full potential.If you have to wonder whether you'll have food or rent, or worry about abuse or crime, then it's difficult to reach your full potential.If you fear you'll go to prison rather than college because of the color of your skin, or that your family will be deported because of your legal status, or that you may be a victim of violence because of your religion, sexual orientation or gender identity, then it's difficult to reach your full potential.We need institutions that understand these issues are all connected. That's the philosophy of the new type of school your mother is building.By partnering with schools, health centers, parent groups and local governments, and by ensuring all children are well fed and cared for starting young, we can start to treat these inequities as connected. Only then can we collectively start to give everyone an equal opportunity.It will take many years to fully develop this model. But it's another example of how advancing human potential and promoting equality are tightly linked. If we want either, we must first build inclusive and healthy communities.• • •For your generation to live in a better world, there is so much more our generation can do.Today your mother and I are committing to spend our lives doing our small part to help solve these challenges. I will continue to serve as Facebook's CEO for many, many years to come, but these issues are too important to wait until you or we are older to begin this work. By starting at a young age, we hope to see compounding benefits throughout our lives.As you begin the next generation of the Chan Zuckerberg family, we also begin the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative to join people across the world to advance human potential and promote equality for all children in the next generation. Our initial areas of focus will be personalized learning, curing disease, connecting people and building strong communities.We will give 99% of our Facebook shares -- currently about $45 billion -- during our lives to advance this mission. We know this is a small contribution compared to all the resources and talents of those already working on these issues. But we want to do what we can, working alongside many others.We'll share more details in the coming months once we settle into our new family rhythm and return from our maternity and paternity leaves. We understand you'll have many questions about why and how we're doing this.As we become parents and enter this next chapter of our lives, we want to share our deep appreciation for everyone who makes this possible.We can do this work only because we have a strong global community behind us. Building Facebook has created resources to improve the world for the next generation. Every member of the Facebook community is playing a part in this work.We can make progress towards these opportunities only by standing on the shoulders of experts -- our mentors, partners and many incredible people whose contributions built these fields.And we can only focus on serving this community and this mission because we are surrounded by loving family, supportive friends and amazing colleagues. We hope you will have such deep and inspiring relationships in your life too.Max, we love you and feel a great responsibility to leave the world a better place for you and all children. We wish you a life filled with the same love, hope and joy you give us. We can't wait to see what you bring to this world.Love,Mom and DadYou use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 'Fight against Gyanesh Kumar will continue': CJP's Dipke targets CEC ahead of anti-SIR rally in Kochi
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday said his party would continue its campaign against Chief Election Commissioner
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday said his party would continue its campaign against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar until an independent and impartial electoral system was ensured in the country.Dipke made the remarks after arriving at Cochin International Airport to attend the party's ‘Jantar Mantar at Kochi’ protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and Kumar.He alleged that elections conducted under the present Chief Election Commissioner could not be trusted."The fight against Gyanesh Kumar will continue until we get an independent and impartial election system in India. That is very necessary because, under Gyanesh Kumar, elections cannot be trusted. They are being rigged only to help one party, and we have seen plenty of examples of that," he alleged.Asked whether votes had been deleted in Keralam during the SIR exercise, Dipke claimed that voter deletions were taking place across the country."Votes are being deleted across the country. There is not even a single state where votes are not being deleted..." he said.He also claimed that more than 13 crore voters had been deleted, accounting for 13-14% of the registered electorate. These figures were his allegations and could not be independently verified from the details available.Dipke said he expected a large turnout of young people, claiming that Keralam had the highest number of registered CJP members."I am pretty sure the young population of Keralam, the youth of Keralam, will come out in large numbers today. From our database, I can definitely tell you that the largest number of registered CJP members are from Keralam," he said.He added that he was attending the protest at the invitation of the organisers and actor Prakash Raj, describing it as a people's movement.Asked about the appointment of the former Keralam chief electoral officer as secretary to the state's chief minister, Dipke said such appointments could raise questions about the impartiality of the electoral system."I think such a thing should not happen anywhere. A similar thing happened in Bengal when the BJP won the election; they appointed the election commissioner as the chief secretary of the CM. These things cannot be entertained or tolerated when it comes to the impartiality of the election system..." he said.The protest rally began at Marine Drive in Kochi, with around 500 activists taking part, organisers said. Led by actor Prakash Raj, the march was organised to demand the withdrawal of the SIR exercise and the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) state president Chintha Jerome also joined the march. articles.title: Digital arrest: A cyberfraud wrapped in a psychological trap; why intelligence falls prey to basic instincts
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Last week, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant expressed exasperation over the growing number of \"digital arrest\" scams, questioning how even
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Last week, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant expressed exasperation over the growing number of "digital arrest" scams, questioning how even educated people continued to fall victim to them despite repeated public awareness campaigns."What is wrong with these victims? How are these victims being trapped like this? They can't understand this basic thing? What's the fear of arrest on mobile?" the CJI orally observed while hearing a suo motu case on digital arrests."Hit the mobile on the wall and arrest goes. Something is wrong with people. God knows what is there. What kind of person are you in a democratic country if you think you are getting arrested on mobile?" he added.But is it really that simple?Every day, people across the country fall victim to these scams. It often begins with an unfamiliar voice on the phone, claiming that the person has been implicated in a crime. What follows is a carefully orchestrated web of threats, intimidation and psychological manipulation, with victims drawn deeper into the trap over phone and video calls.No legal basis for digital arrestAs society evolves, so does crime. While traditional theft involved breaking into homes, cracking safes or carrying out armed robberies, the expansion of digital technology has opened up new avenues for criminals. Increasingly, fraudsters no longer need to come face to face with their victims to rob them.Digital arrest is one such sophisticated form of cyber fraud. Criminals impersonate police officers or officials of investigative agencies, convincing unsuspecting people that they are under investigation for serious offences.Typically, the scam begins with a phone or video call in which fraudsters claim that the victim's identity has been linked to crimes such as money laundering, drug trafficking or other illegal activities.Victims are then made to believe that they are under constant surveillance and instructed to remain on video calls for hours, sometimes even days, without contacting family members or anyone else. To lend credibility to their claims, scammers often produce forged arrest warrants, court orders and official-looking identity documents, making the threat of legal action appear genuine.The intimidation eventually gives way to demands for money. Victims are instructed to transfer funds to designated bank accounts for supposed verification, security clearance or to avoid arrest.But digital arrest has no legal basis. No law enforcement agency can arrest someone over a video call or demand money to prevent prosecution. Nor do authorities issue or serve arrest warrants through video calls, WhatsApp, emails or other messaging platforms.The magnitude of digital arrestsThe scale of the problem is reflected in government data. According to a 2025 response in the Rajya Sabha, reported digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes in India nearly tripled between 2022 and 2024, while the amount defrauded increased more than 21-fold.Replying to a parliamentary question, minister of state for home affairs Bandi Sanjay Kumar furnished data on digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes reported on the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal (NCRP) over the three-year period.The data showed that 39,925 incidents were reported in 2022, involving a total defrauded amount of Rs 91.14 crore. By 2024, the number of reported incidents had risen to 1,23,672, while the amount defrauded had surged to Rs 1,935.51 crore.The growing sophistication and scale of these scams have also drawn the attention of the Supreme Court.In October 2025, the court took suo motu cognizance of the issue after a senior citizen couple from Haryana approached it, alleging that fraudsters posing as investigative agency officials had cheated them of more than Rs 1 crore using forged court documents.Investigations have also brought into focus the organised networks operating behind these frauds, including syndicates based overseas. A major challenge for investigators is tracing the money trail, with criminals using intermediary or "mule" bank accounts to receive stolen funds and rapidly transfer them across multiple accounts to evade detection.More than digital, it's psychologicalThe persistence of these scams raises an important question: Why do some people fall for something that may appear obviously fraudulent to others?Speaking to The Times of India, clinical psychologist Yukta Sharma said phishing and cyberfraud should not be dismissed as instances of poor judgement. Instead, they exploit ordinary human responses to fear, uncertainty, authority and the promise of rewards."Phishing is not merely a technological problem. The technology provides the medium, but the actual vulnerability being exploited is often human psychology," Sharma said, adding that even people who are intellectually well-equipped can fall prey to such traps.According to her, scammers deliberately create situations designed to provoke an immediate emotional response. This could be fear of losing money, anxiety over possible legal consequences, excitement about a potential reward or trust in someone posing as an authority figure."When an individual is being targeted through a phishing attempt, there is often a complex interplay of emotional arousal, cognitive processing and decision-making taking place. These attacks deliberately create situations that trigger an immediate emotional response, whether it is fear of losing money, anxiety about legal consequences, excitement over a potential reward or trust in an apparently legitimate authority," she said."Once these emotions are activated, the individual's attention tends to become increasingly focused on resolving the perceived situation rather than questioning its authenticity," Sharma told TOI.She explained that victims may move gradually from initial suspicion to compliance as fraudsters build credibility through convincing explanations, repeated instructions and sustained pressure.By the time the deception is exposed, victims are often left dealing with shock, disbelief, guilt, embarrassment and anxiety. The experience can be particularly distressing because they may struggle to understand how they were manipulated into surrendering their money.India's fight against digital arrestsA NITI Aayog report describes cybercrime in India as having evolved from a "distant threat into a pervasive everyday reality". Recognising the growing challenge, the Centre has stepped up efforts to combat digital fraud and strengthen the country's cybercrime response.One of the key initiatives is the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), established by the ministry of home affairs to coordinate national efforts to tackle cybercrime and support its prevention and investigation.To address financial cyber fraud, the government launched the financial cyber fraud reporting system in 2021, enabling victims to report incidents quickly. According to the report, the system has helped save more than Rs 3,431 crore across 9.94 lakh complaints.The government has also strengthened cyber forensic capabilities through the National Cyber Forensic Laboratory in Delhi and the Evidence Lab in Hyderabad, enhancing the ability of law enforcement agencies to examine and analyse digital evidence.The I4C's online training platform, CyTrain, meanwhile, aims to equip police personnel and judicial officers with the skills required to investigate and prosecute cybercrime.The Reserve Bank of India is also exploring the possibility of introducing a 'kill switch' mechanism that would allow potential victims to immediately block all financial transactions from their accounts.But are these measures enough to keep pace with increasingly sophisticated cybercriminals?Former Bihar director general of police Abhyanand believes digital arrest scams must be treated as serious cases of organised cheating, requiring a specialised and professional police response.Speaking to TOI, he said cybercrime has traditionally been one of the weaker areas of policing, largely because perpetrators are difficult to trace and may operate across state or international borders."Digital arrest is a sophisticated form of cheating and the police must treat it as such. It is a combination of cybercrime and traditional fraud. Cybercrime has traditionally been one of the weak areas for the police, as it is often difficult to trace the source of the crime. The perpetrators could be operating from another state or even another country," the former DGP said."To tackle such cases effectively, the police need specialised training and must approach these investigations with professionalism," he added.Cyber and privacy law expert advocate Prashant Mali, meanwhile, argued that India needs stronger financial surveillance, more accountable telecom infrastructure and faster action against fraudulent accounts to tackle the menace."I feel we need stronger financial surveillance, accountable telecom infrastructure, faster freezing of fraudulent accounts, international cooperation and effective law enforcement," Mali told TOI.He also criticised the lack of effective deterrence against cybercriminals, arguing that convictions in cybercrime cases remain in single digits."I feel government is not able to create deterrence in the minds of cyber criminals engaged in the brutal digital arrest, cyber crime. We need to make an example of the crime digital arrest related convictions, but the convictions in cybercrime matters are in single figures," he said.Mali also proposed a government-backed insurance mechanism to protect victims of digital fraud, arguing that the financial burden should not fall on those who have already been cheated. "I feel government asked for digital India as the flagship program. Now digital arrest is the fallout where unsuspecting victims are falling prey to fraud. We need digital India insurance for digital arrest victims where the premium is paid by government and banking, financial services, and insurance participants and not by the victim. Every Indian should be secured from a digital accident like the digital arrest by Digital India Insurance," he suggested.As India pushes ahead with its digital transformation, cybercriminals are finding increasingly sophisticated ways to exploit the same technology. The fight against digital arrest scams, therefore, cannot rest on awareness campaigns or individual vigilance alone. It will require better-trained police forces, stronger financial safeguards, faster investigations and a system that can respond as swiftly as the fraudsters operate.The CJI's question about why people continue to fall for these scams is important. But the answer lies not simply in telling victims to be more careful. It lies in understanding how fear and manipulation can override rational judgement, and building institutions capable of protecting people when that happens.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Find a new wife: Katie Miller reacts to news report detailing her 'lobbying' for husband Miller's promotion to Susie Wiles' job
articles.summary: After President Donald Trump fired Susie Wiles and promoted Stephen Miller to the post of chief of staff, POLITICO reported on the behind-the-scenes that
articles.body: After President Donald Trump fired Susie Wiles and promoted Stephen Miller to the post of chief of staff, POLITICO reported on the behind-the-scenes that included a lot of apparent lobbying from his wife, Katie Miller. Katie told contacts to call Trump on Stephen’s behalf if they believed he was a better choice than other potential successors to Susie Wiles, the report claimed.Among the names Trump privately discussed over the past month were Federal Housing Finance Agency Director Bill Pulte, special envoy Steve Witkoff, former House Speaker Kevin McCarthy and New York Yankees president Randy Levine. Lee Zeldin and Sergio Gor were also considered. The names have been doing the rounds for quite some time. President Trump initially denied the rumors and said the speculation was 100% false. But Katie continued lobbying.Katie worked at the Department of Homeland Security during Trump's first administration and served on the White House coronavirus task force. During his second term, she worked with Elon Musk on the Department of Government Efficiency initiative before launching a podcast that featured senior administration officials.Her campaign to secure the position for her husband gained momentum after the midterm elections. She made around half a dozen calls to people close to Trump, including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and several individuals connected to Vice President JD Vance, the POLITICO report said.While the report mentioned that Katie declined to comment, Katie posted her comment on X referring to the article and stated that it was just a wife supporting her husband. And if people don't have that, they should get a new wife."BREAKING: Wife supports husband. If your wife doesn’t do this, find a new one," Katie posted, sharing the POLITICO article.'If Wiles were to leave...'Katie sent out a message that if Susie Wiles were to leave, it would have to be Stephen Miller for the job. Stephen was the deputy chief of staff and the mind behind Trump's (anti-) immigration policies. People familiar with her outreach said Katie had never advocated for Wiles' removal. They added that her latest round of calls this week came only after it became clear that Trump was ready to appoint a new chief of staff."He started telling people he was done with Susie," the person with direct knowledge said, referring to Trump's reaction after the election. "This is what happens when you get creamed."Trump's final round of calls was after Election DayFrustration with Wiles in sections of the White House had been building throughout the midterm campaign. However, the Republicans' unexpectedly humiliating defeat on Tuesday night appeared to seal her fate.Trump called several allies in the days following the election, expressing anger over some of his top advisers, including Wiles and her allies, according to two people close to the White House. "There was just no saving Susie. She knew that," one of them said.Wiles, who recently underwent chemotherapy for breast cancer, had herself been considering leaving after the midterms, according to two other people close to the White House."She loves the job — it's the job of a lifetime, but you have no life," one of them said. "She's sick of like — having drinks and then going back to work."Katie had begun receiving calls from people within the White House and Trump's allies as early as October, asking about the possibility of Wiles leaving. During those conversations, she suggested that they support Stephen as a potential replacement.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 100 days adrift in the Pacific Ocean: Nine family members leave Micronesia for a one-hour boat trip to collect supplies, but a storm carries them over 3,000 miles to Kiribati, where five survive and four die
articles.summary: What was supposed to be a one-hour boat journey turned into a nearly 100-day fight for survival in the Pacific Ocean.
articles.body: What was supposed to be a one-hour boat journey turned into a nearly 100-day fight for survival in the Pacific Ocean. Nine family members from Micronesia found themselves stranded aboard a 20-foot skiff after a storm blew their boat off course and it ran out of fuel. With no immediate rescue in sight, they battled hunger, dehydration and harsh weather for months. Four family members, including a child, died during the ordeal, while the five survivors eventually reached an island in Kiribati, more than 3,000 miles away.A short journey turns into a nightmare at seaAccording to reports by The New York Times, The Times and the Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC), the family boarded the small boat on July 30. Among the nine passengers were 31-year-old Tedwinson Paul and eight younger relatives. They were travelling between islands in Micronesia to collect supplies, expecting to complete the journey in about an hour.However, a storm changed everything. The boat was blown off course and eventually ran out of fuel, leaving the family at the mercy of the ocean. Arthur Irons II, an official from Chuuk, the Micronesian state from which the family had departed, told The New York Times that he alerted the federal government after learning that the group had gone missing.The US Coast Guard subsequently launched a search operation. However, after several days, the search was called off, leaving the family to continue their desperate struggle for survival.Four relatives die as survivors struggle to stay aliveAs their time at sea stretched from days into weeks, the family faced increasingly difficult conditions. According to The New York Times, four of the nine passengers, including a child, died during the journey.The five survivors were reportedly forced to throw their deceased relatives overboard. With limited food and no access to fresh drinking water, they relied on whatever they could find to stay alive.The family reportedly caught and ate turtles and birds, while rainwater became their main source of drinking water. They also tried to attract attention by waving at passing ships and aircraft, hoping someone would spot them and come to their rescue. However, their attempts went unanswered.How the five family members reached an island in KiribatiAfter almost 100 days adrift, the survivors finally spotted land. Their boat had travelled more than 3,000 miles before reaching Fanning Island, part of Kiribati, on November 1.The journey ended when the small skiff ran aground on the island's coral-filled shoreline and was destroyed. The five survivors, identified in reports as three men and two teenage boys, then made their way towards a nearby village.They reportedly followed the sound of church bells, which eventually led them to local residents. The villagers initially struggled to understand their condition and thought they were intoxicated because they could barely walk. It soon became apparent that the group needed urgent medical attention.The survivors were reportedly found naked, malnourished and severely dehydrated after spending months at sea. A local church pastor took them in and helped ensure they received care.Survivors show signs of recovery after rescueBy November 2, the five family members were beginning to recover. Nursing officer Paukin Tororo told the ABC that their condition had improved and they were showing signs of responding to treatment.“They can move their head side by side,” Tororo said. “They can give a smile face, they show the sign they want to eat.”The update brought some relief after the harrowing rescue, although the loss of four family members remained a devastating part of the ordeal.Alexander Narruhn, the governor of Chuuk, confirmed on November 1 that discussions had begun with the Kiribati government to arrange the survivors' return home, according to the Associated Press.The US Coast Guard also welcomed the news that five people had been found and were receiving care. In a statement to PEOPLE, the agency said, “We are extremely relieved to hear that five individuals were found and are receiving care based on media reports. We extend our profound condolences for those who are still missing.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Nikki Haley's analysis of GOP's midterm loss: 'You can't blame media, you can't blame academia, you can't blame Hollywood'; Son Nalin Haley agrees
articles.summary: Former US ambassador to the United Nations Nikki Haley has urged Republicans to accept responsibility for their sweeping losses in the midterm elections,
articles.body: Former US ambassador to the United Nations Nikki Haley has urged Republicans to accept responsibility for their sweeping losses in the midterm elections, saying the party failed to listen to voters and focus on their everyday concerns. Appearing on NBC's Today show on Wednesday, Haley told Republicans not to blame the media, academia or Hollywood for the defeat, arguing that these institutions had opposed the party for years but had not prevented it from winning elections in the past."To my fellow Republicans, this is not the time to whine, complain, or point fingers. You can't blame media, you can't blame academia, you can't blame Hollywood," Haley said. "All of those have been against us for years before, and we've won. The bottom line is, Republicans didn't listen to the American people; they listened to Washington, DC," she added.Haley said voters repeatedly raised concerns about the cost of living, including high grocery bills, fuel prices and healthcare expenses, but Republicans failed to address them."And while the American people were saying groceries are high, gas is high, healthcare is high, you're not listening," she said.She also criticized what she described as a culture of self-interest and corruption in Washington, saying Republican leaders had become disconnected from the concerns of ordinary Americans. "What you saw in DC was self-dealing and corruption and celebrating," she said.Urging her party to regroup rather than dwell on the defeat, Haley said: "Get a good night's sleep, take our medicine, and let's get to work."She argued that Republicans could recover before the next election cycle but would have to shift their focus towards issues that matter to voters. "This can shift in two years, but you have got to start focusing on what the American people want and not these issues in D.C. that nobody cares about," she said.Haley also had a warning for Democrats, who made significant gains in the midterm elections. "Now, for our Democrats: you can celebrate, but be careful what you wish for," she said, pointing to the election of several candidates she described as democratic socialists."I think both parties need to do some self-reflecting and see where they decide to go, because two years, a lot can change again in two years," she said.Vivek-critic Nalin Haley agrees, says Democrats didn't winNikki Haley's son Nalin Haley, who made a foray into MAGA commentary and thereby despised politicians like Vivek Ramaswamy too, offered a similar analysis: Democrats didn't win, Republicans los"If Republicans don’t take this as*-whooping as a time to self-reflect, then it will be wasted. Democrats didn’t win, Republicans lost!""We primarily lost not cuz of what we did, but what we didn’t do. We had control of the house, senate, and presidency. What did we do with it? Nothing! When we did act, it was tone deaf and only catered to the needs of elites and foreign governments, not everyday working Americans," he said."We are not going to elect republicans for the sake of locking democrats out. That’s not enough. We elect them cuz we expect them to put our country and its people first. That starts by being honest, reflecting, and holding OUR party and OUR Republicans accountable for what they did and what they didn’t do!" he added.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: White House unveils new design for Trump's 250-foot triumphal arch amid 14-day halt
articles.summary: The White House reveals new designs for President Trump's planned Military Triumphal Arch, highlighting its tribute to U.S. military history, as legal challenges temporarily pause construction.
articles.body: The White House has released fresh designs for President Donald Trump's proposed 250-foot triumphal arch in Washington, presenting the project as a tribute to America's military history as construction faces a temporary court-ordered halt.The new visuals, shared on Friday, show three gilded statues with wings positioned above the words “GOLDEN AGE OF AMERICA”. One of the figures holds a torch with a flame emerging from it. The structure is planned near the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery, across the Potomac River from Washington.The project is now being promoted as the Military Triumphal Arch on a website launched by the United States Triumphal Arch Foundation. The White House shared the new renderings from the organisation, whose chairman, Randy Evans, a former ambassador appointed during Trump's presidency, said the foundation operates independently of the federal government.The latest presentation comes as the proposal faces legal challenges over its location and potential impact on the surrounding landscape. Virginia Attorney General and District of Columbia officials have filed a lawsuit seeking to stop construction, arguing that the structure would permanently affect the Washington skyline and nearby landmarks, including Arlington National Cemetery and the Lincoln Memorial.A federal judge on Thursday issued a 14-day restraining order preventing construction from moving forward. US District Judge Tanya Chutkan said the project could disrupt traffic, generate noise and require extensive excavation, among other effects. The order followed approval of the proposal by the National Capital Planning Commission, which voted in favour of the project after hearing objections from around 100 people, including Democratic lawmakers.The Trump administration has argued that Congress authorised the arch more than a century ago, when it approved the construction of a bridge across the Potomac River. The legal dispute will determine whether that earlier approval provides sufficient authority for the proposed structure.White House spokesman Davis Ingle criticised the court's intervention, describing the ruling as the decision of an “activist district court”. He said the administration expected to prevail as the legal proceedings continued.“We are confident we will be fully vindicated as this litigation proceeds and look forward to seeing the completion of this magnificent Arch, a tribute to 250 years of American greatness,” Ingle said on Friday as cited by Reuters.Trump had previously described the proposed arch as a “military complex” intended to accommodate drones and snipers. The new designs place greater emphasis on its symbolic role, presenting it as a monument to the country's military heritage.The proposal is among several major construction and renovation projects Trump has pursued in Washington. His plans have attracted opposition from lawmakers, officials and preservation advocates, with the arch becoming the subject of both political debate and legal proceedings.You use AI every day. articles.title: Balochistan Parties call statewide shutdown in mid-November as crisis deepens in troubled province
articles.summary: Political parties in Pakistan’s Balochistan province have called a province-wide shutdown strike for November 19, to be followed by demonstrations at
articles.body: Political parties in Pakistan’s Balochistan province have called a province-wide shutdown strike for November 19, to be followed by demonstrations at district headquarters. They accuse the provincial and federal governments of failing to address mounting security, political and economic concerns.The decision was taken at an all-parties conference organised by the Awami National Party (ANP) at the Quetta Press Club, according to a report by The Express Tribune cited by ANI. ANP provincial president Asghar Khan Achakzai chaired the meeting, which was attended by representatives of the National Party, Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam, Pashtunkhwa National Awami Party and several other political groups. The participants agreed to bring their joint political and democratic efforts under a coordinated movement to raise public grievances.In a joint declaration, the parties described the situation in Balochistan as alarming. They cited persistent insecurity, terrorism, extremism, armed group activities, targeted killings and kidnappings for ransom. They also raised the unresolved issue of missing persons, and highlighted the difficulties faced by transporters and passengers travelling on national highways.The parties pointed to rising unemployment and economic decline. They blamed the closure of trade and transit routes with Afghanistan and Iran for disrupting economic activity across the province. Soaring inflation, prolonged power and gas outages, petroleum levies and restrictions on the supply of essential agricultural inputs, including urea fertiliser, were also cited. According to The Express Tribune, the leaders said these issues had adversely affected agriculture, trade, industries and employment.The participating parties also criticised the provincial and federal governments, accusing them of failing to ensure public safety, maintain law and order, protect natural resources and restore economic stability.Furthermore, the parties announced a provincial-level meeting on November 26 to decide the next course of action. An all-parties conference will be held in the first week of December to take Balochistan’s concerns to the national leadership.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Kashmir-linked outfit claims responsibility in Ghaziabad police outpost blast; UP ATS probes possible terror angle
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: The Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) has taken the lead in investigating the explosion outside the Vasundhara police outpost in
articles.body: LUCKNOW: The Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) has taken the lead in investigating the explosion outside the Vasundhara police outpost in Ghaziabad's Indirapuram area, amid indications of a possible terror angle after a little-known Kashmir-linked outfit claimed responsibility through a social media post.Investigators are also examining a suspicious Delhi-registered scooter found near the scene.An ATS team headed by DIG Abhishek Yadav reached the spot on Saturday soon after the incident and began a joint probe with the bomb disposal squad, forensic experts and local police. Security agencies are scrutinising whether an explosive device was hurled at the outpost from the adjoining elevated road.The blast occurred around 9pm on Friday, on the eve of Dhanteras, near the police outpost under Indirapuram police station limits.While the explosion caused damage to the outpost, including shattered windowpanes, damaged air-conditioners and cracks in a wall, no police personnel were injured. A sub-inspector present inside the outpost at the time escaped unharmed.However, Vishal, a 20-year-old food delivery executive from Arthala who was passing by the outpost, sustained minor injuries. He was treated and is reported to be stable.The investigation gathered momentum after an X account named "Ghazi-2" circulated a purported claim of responsibility on behalf of an outfit calling itself Tehreek-ul-Mujahideen Hindustan.The group allegedly released a video showing a masked individual speaking in Urdu and Hindi and claiming that the attack was aimed at the police. An English-language statement accompanied the video.Sources familiar with the probe said the outfit is largely unknown to security agencies but bears similarities to networks allegedly linked to Pakistan-based operative Shehzad Bhatti. Investigators are examining whether the claim has connections to the ISI-Bhatti network.Bhatti had previously floated a similarly named outfit, Tehreek-e-Taliban Hindustan (TTH), which had issued threats and claimed attacks targeting police personnel and stations in Punjab. Notably, the UP ATS had recently cracked down on an alleged Bhatti-linked module operating in the state, a case later transferred to the National Investigation Agency (NIA).The social media account that uploaded the video and statement was reportedly deleted shortly after the posts surfaced. Cyber experts are now tracing the origin of the content and verifying the authenticity of the claim.One of the key focus areas of the probe is the elevated road running near the outpost. Preliminary findings suggest an explosive object may have been thrown from the approximately 35-foot-high stretch towards the outpost below.CCTV footage from the elevated corridor and surrounding areas is being analysed to identify suspicious movement before and after the blast.Meanwhile, forensic teams have collected samples from the site, and officials said the exact nature of the explosion would be known only after scientific examination of the evidence.Officials said all angles, including sabotage and accidental ignition, remain under examination.The area remains cordoned off as ATS, forensic and local police teams continue efforts to establish the source of the blast and identify those behind it.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: Healthcare, Iran war & tariffs: Resurgent Democrats set stage to confront Trump
articles.summary: With Democrats securing a majority in both the houses of US Congress, the party is preparing to roll back several key policies of President Donald Trump,
articles.body: With Democrats securing a majority in both the houses of US Congress, the party is preparing to roll back several key policies of President Donald Trump, putting healthcare cuts, the war with Iran and trade tariffs at the centre of its legislative agenda.Democrats are planning to use their expanded strength in Congress to push legislation reversing Republican-backed Medicaid cuts, restore subsidies for millions of Americans buying health insurance and challenge Trump's handling of the Iran war.According to a report by the Associated Press, Democratic leaders are preparing to move quickly when the new Congress convenes on January 3, with early votes expected to focus on reversing Republican-backed Medicaid cuts and restoring enhanced tax subsidies under the Affordable Care Act (ACA). It helps millions of Americans afford health insurance.Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries has made it clear that the party intends to move quickly on its promises.“We’re going to get out of the gate fast,” Jeffries said, signalling an early push on healthcare, Iran and Trump's trade policies.Jeffries said Democrats would prioritise reversing Medicaid cuts, extending Affordable Care Act tax credits and ending what he called the “reckless and costly war of choice in Iran”. He argued that the conflict had pushed up fuel prices, adding to the financial burden on American households.Democratic leaders have also made clear that they are prepared for a confrontation with the White House if Trump refuses to back their proposals.Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said the party would continue pushing its agenda even if the president blocks the legislation. “If he vetoes it, it will show the divisions,” Schumer said in an interview with The New York Times podcast The Daily.Schumer also indicated that Democrats could find support among some Republicans on restoring enhanced tax subsidies for ACA plans. Asked about the possibility of bipartisan cooperation, he said he was receiving “initial signs” of willingness from some Republicans on certain issues.What Democrats' takeover means for TrumpFor Trump, the Democratic takeover of both chambers of Congress could mean two difficult final years of his presidency, with his administration facing legislative challenges, investigations and increased scrutiny of its policies.Democrats will control the congressional agenda, lead key committees and have greater powers to summon administration officials for hearings, putting several aspects of Trump's presidency under greater scrutiny.The Iran war could become one of the biggest sources of confrontation. Democrats are preparing to challenge the president's handling of the conflict through war powers legislation, while rising fuel prices linked to the war have emerged as a political liability.Trump has acknowledged that the conflict affected the midterm results, with Vice-President JD Vance also blaming the war for Republican losses.However, Trump retains his presidential veto, and Democrats will still face hurdles in the Senate, including the 60-vote threshold for most legislation. This means that while Democrats can pass bills in the House and intensify scrutiny of the administration, turning their proposals into law could prove difficult.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump says ‘I just wanted to make a change’ as Stephen Miller replaces Susie Wiles as chief of staff
articles.summary: In a significant leadership change, President Trump replaces Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller as Chief of Staff, aiming to energize his administration following recent Republican electoral losses. Miller's rise underscores the ongoing focus on immigration policies.
articles.body: President Donald Trump has appointed longtime adviser Stephen Miller as his new White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles in a leadership change that follows Republicans' setbacks in the midterm elections.Speaking to reporters on Friday, Trump said he wanted a change, while praising Wiles' performance in the role. “I think Susie's done a very good job, great job, but I just wanted to make a change,” he said. “Stephen's been great. And we've got to make moves. Sometimes, sometimes in life, you have to make moves.”Trump announced the appointment in a Truth Social post, describing Miller as one of his “most trusted advisors”. Miller is due to take over the position on Monday. Wiles, who will move to the Trump Political Operation, was thanked by the president for her service.Wiles submitted her resignation to Trump on Thursday night, a US official and a senior White House adviser told CBS News. Three sources familiar with the matter linked her departure to the Republican Party's midterm losses. It was not immediately clear whether her deputies would remain in the administration.Wiles had initially planned to continue as chief of staff through Congress' lame-duck session, with her departure expected towards the end of the year or early next year. Trump brought forward that timeline.Miller has held several influential responsibilities in the administration, most notably shaping Trump's immigration enforcement and deportation policies. Trump described him as “very good politically” and a “great manager” when speaking to reporters.Wiles had managed Trump's 2024 presidential campaign before becoming his chief of staff when he returned to the White House. In an X post, she described serving in the administration as the honour of a lifetime and listed border security, tax cuts and economic policy among the administration's achievements.“While my role may be changing, my commitment to the president and the mission never will,” Wiles wrote, adding that she was grateful to the people she had worked alongside.Miller also acknowledged Wiles' departure, thanking her as “the incomparable Susie Wiles”. He said the administration's mission was “more clear than ever” and pledged to continue supporting Trump.The appointment places a central figure behind the administration's immigration agenda in one of the White House's most senior positions. Miller's promotion also signals Trump's intention to maintain his governing approach despite the electoral losses suffered by Republicans.Democratic lawmakers have strongly opposed Miller's policies, and his elevation is likely to intensify tensions as the party prepares to take control of Congress in January. The appointment comes despite Trump's recent comments that he believes he can work with the incoming Democratic leadership.House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is expected to become speaker, called Miller a “dangerous xenophobe and reckless extremist”. He also said Miller's presence in government should be “eradicated like a malignant tumor”.​You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Trumpiana: POTUS LOTUS grumpus ‘veto-us’
articles.summary: Pool pool on the mall, who’s the greatest loser of them all?
articles.body: Pool pool on the mall, who’s the greatest loser of them all?As the midnight massacre of red Republicans turned Washington’s Reflecting Pool deep Democratic blue, Donald Trump turned a petulant “Political Pundit, both good and bad,” to find scapegoats for the stinging rebuke.For once, POTUS 45& 47 who had undertaken a 3o-state blistering blitz over 32 days to fire up his MAGA base exhorting them to pretend he was on the ballot— 47 times by a New York Times count — was “absolutely willing” to accept the election results — but the blame, no way!“I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” declared an unfazed Trump on Truth Social blaming everyone from individual candidates to even Fox News but himself, as the Republicans rout robbed them of control of both chambers of the Congress.As the writing on the wall became clear on election night, Trump told the Times he looked forward to working with Democrats even as he flexed his veto muscles. “I have total veto power, so they have to come to us,” he said. “And if they have some good ideas, I’m certainly open to working.”While his Vice President JD Vance suggested on X that the “real reason” for the Republican’s widespread losses was anger over Iran war, Trump himself had no regrets for a “very wise decision for the future of the country and the world” saying he “would do that again.”He acknowledged that voters were unhappy about gas prices. “They don’t mind the Iran, but they probably weren’t happy — they weren’t happy with the oil price,” Trump said.But he insisted that he regretted nothing about the first two years of his second term, despite the widespread Republican defeats. “I consider it to be the most successful two-year period in the history of any president,” he told the Times.And as Trump’s enemies and frenemies at home and abroad gleefully viewed him as a “hobbled duck,” he lost no time in declaring a new war with a photo of a red baseball cap with just one word “VETO” followed by another of a glaring Trump reminding everyone, “PSA: TRUMP IS STILL YOUR PRESIDENT.”Then as Friday rolled in Trump replaced his “Ice Maiden” chief of staff Susie Wiles with her deputy Stephen Miller, a key architect of his tough immigration crackdown and other provocative policies, signalling his intention to double down on his hard-line MAGA agenda with an aggressive approach to executive power.And while liberal critics lamented the “exit of another powerful woman,” Trump announced wily Wiles, a key architect of his own 2024 victory, will be moving over to the Trump Political Operation, signalling that he wasn’t going to loosen his hold on Republican party any time soon.With the curtain finally down on the most expensive midterm elections with ultra wealthy donors spending an estimated $2 billion with tech titan Elon Musk alone contributing $474 million to Republican groups, candidates and their allies, Trump returned to more pressing matters of state — like making Washington beautiful again.Less than 24 hours after the Republican rout, Trump was back boasting about his big beautiful ballroom, rhapsodizing about its “magnificent” columns carved out of limestone, 50ft-high ceilings, ability to hold more than 300 guests, heavy-set beams, “drone-proof” roof, thick marble floors and military-grade bunker.“The whole thing is a miracle, and it’s all because of you,” Trump told gathered reporters and network TV cameras at a White House event to congratulate his team making no mention of Democrats’ ‘blue wave’ for more than 20 minutes.“Look, I’ll get along probably with the Democrats, unless they want to be destructive, but I have the power of the veto,” Trump said when he finally got round to answering questions.It was a fitting finale to the campaign for Trump who chose to make his last pitch to voters at the Reflecting Pool, touting his troubled $14 million renovation project and accusing his bêtes noires Barack Obama and Joe Biden of neglecting the Washington landmark.Holding up a blown-up photo of the pool before he cleaned it up, Trump said, “The algae is brutal. It forms easily … All you saw was dirt and filth and paper and everything else for years.”And then as Trump quickly won approval for his controversial 250-foot-high “Triumphal Arch” from a planning commission led by his own appointees, a desi federal judge promptly blocked its construction for 14 days.Back in the White House, Trump signed a proclamation declaring his gilded Oval Office a “national monument” — to his blunderbuss rule — to preserve his kitschy renovations as a “landmark for the ages.”His first executive act after the midterm drubbing “would ensure the West Wing rooms would not be “touched by anybody, destroyed, ripped down by stupid people, in order to build something in a slightly different shape,” he declared sitting behind the Resolute Desk.On the desk next to him sat a red baseball cap emblazoned with the word “Veto” – an explicit reminder of how he planned to confront the new Democratic-controlled Congress next year. He followed it up with his glaring picture in black and white proclaiming ‘Mr Veto.’Earlier on the result night, as shadows lengthened outside, Trump complaining, “It’s so dark outside, so early…Isn’t that ridiculous?” vowed to“keep fighting” for year-round daylight saving time. “Just a few days ago it was so nice and sunny at this same time,” he reminisced nostalgically.Alas, all the king’s executive fiats and all the king’s vetoes can’t put the clock back on the midterm blues!(By arrangement with The American Bazaar) You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Iron Gate': US forms special task force to restrict Iran's land exports
articles.summary: Moving beyond the naval blockade, the US central command on Saturday announced the creation of a special task force to prevent Iran from using land routes
articles.body: Moving beyond the naval blockade, the US central command on Saturday announced the creation of a special task force to prevent Iran from using land routes and the Caspian Sea to transport advanced weapons, sanctioned materials and other “restricted” goods.According to Centcom commander Admiral Brad Cooper, “Task Force Iron Gate” will comprise around 20 civilian and military personnel. It will operate from Tampa, Florida, and coordinate with other US government agencies to disrupt the movement of weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials and illegal revenue streams across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea."The establishment of Task Force Iron Gate reinforces the success of our ironclad blockade against Iran at sea," Cooper said."Strengthening CENTCOM's collaboration with U.S. interagency partners will further constrain Iran's ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, and replenish their military," he added.The announcement comes as Washington continues enforcing a naval blockade targeting shipping linked to Iranian ports.According to Centcom, the blockade has prevented Iran from exporting more than $25 billion worth of crude oil in recent months. It said restrictions remain in place on all vessels entering or leaving Iranian ports.On Saturday, Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Spokesperson Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi claimed Tehran was exporting defence equipment like Arman missiles, the 358 loitering munition and the Khordad-3 air defence system, while also meeting domestic demands.“Today, in addition to meeting domestic needs, we have become an exporter of defence equipment and products—a significant achievement for the country,” Mohebbi said.“If another war breaks out, the world will witness the IRGC Aerospace Force’s new capabilities, and our enemies will be astonished by its strength and power,” he added.Centcom said the new initiative would support ongoing US government efforts to prevent Iran from using overland routes to move advanced weapons and other materials.You use AI every day.
