articles.title: Cyndi Lauper joined Ariana DeBose, Darren Criss and Bernadette Peters at a New York charity gala that raised over $750,000 for animal rescue and other nonprofits, taking the event's two-year total past $1.2 million
articles.summary: Cyndi Lauper, Ariana DeBose, Darren Criss and Bernadette Peters came together at the 2026 Fetch Pet Gala in New York City, turning a night of music and
articles.body: Cyndi Lauper, Ariana DeBose, Darren Criss and Bernadette Peters came together at the 2026 Fetch Pet Gala in New York City, turning a night of music and theatre into a major fundraising effort for animal rescue. The event, hosted by Fetch Pet Insurance at The Carlyle Hotel, raised more than $750,000 for four nonprofits, bringing the gala’s two-year total to more than $1.2 million, according to PR Newswire.The evening was built around the idea that pets deserve more than a photo opportunity. It combined live performances, a green carpet featuring adoptable dogs and a push to connect shelter animals with families who can give them a permanent home.A night of performance and purposeThe 2026 Fetch Pet Gala featured performances from Tony and Academy Award winners Bernadette Peters, Darren Criss and Ariana DeBose, along with a surprise appearance by Cyndi Lauper. The event was hosted by Fetch Pet Insurance and sponsored by SATELLAI, an AI-powered pet wellbeing company.The gala’s purpose was clear from the start. It brought together pet industry leaders, animal welfare advocates and celebrity guests for an evening that celebrated the human-animal bond while raising money for pets in need.The $750,000 raised at this year’s event will support four organisations: Broadway Cares/Equity Fights AIDS, Broadway Barks, Wags and Walks, and North Shore Animal League America.The two-year totalThe 2026 gala was the second annual Fetch Pet Gala, and its fundraising total pushed the event’s cumulative impact past $1.2 million in just two years. Paul Guyardo, president and chief executive of Fetch Pet Insurance, said the star power of the gala is what has made that possible.He described the organisations supported by the gala as literally saving lives and delivering meaningful impact for pets in need. That framing reflects the event’s broader mission, which goes beyond a single night of entertainment.The two-year total is a sign that the gala is building momentum. What began as a one-night fundraiser is now establishing itself as a recurring platform for animal welfare advocacy in New York.Adoptable dogs took the spotlightOne of the most visible parts of the evening was the presence of adoptable dogs from North Shore Animal League America, who wore SATELLAI Collar Go devices on the green carpet. The dogs were photographed ahead of the gala in a professional shoot by Stronger Shot, a nationwide initiative that uses photography and storytelling to help shelter pets find homes.Adam Goldberg, founder of Stronger Shot, said the goal was to help people see shelter pets for who they really are, beyond their circumstances. Seeing the dogs go from a shelter photo session to the gala’s green carpet, he said, showed what can happen when brands come together to make adoption more visible and impactful.The collaboration also extended beyond the event itself. SATELLAI is giving five pet parents who adopt a dog from North Shore Animal League America a complimentary Collar Go device, extending the gala’s mission into the weeks and months after adoption.What SATELLAI brought to the tableSATELLAI, founded by pet lovers including members of the founding team whose own experiences with beloved pets shaped the company’s mission, builds technology to help people better understand and care for their pets. The company’s focus is on pet wellbeing, combining AI, smart wearables, sensors, positioning and connectivity to turn everyday pet data into insights about behavior, activity and wellbeing.Mark Mao, founder and chief executive of SATELLAI, said the company was proud to extend its mission beyond the gala by providing Collar Go devices to families adopting dogs from North Shore Animal League America. He described the event as a way to bring the pet community together around the human-animal bond.The company’s involvement shows how a tech brand can use a charity gala to do more than promote a product. By tying its devices to real adoption outcomes, SATELLAI made its sponsorship part of the solution rather than just part of the scenery.The four nonprofits supportedThe $750,000 raised at the 2026 gala will be split among four organisations. Broadway Cares/Equity Fights AIDS supports people in the performing arts community facing health crises, while Broadway Barks focuses on animal adoption and welfare.Wags and Walks is a rescue organisation that places dogs and cats in permanent homes, and North Shore Animal League America is one of the largest no-kill animal rescue and adoption organisations in the country. Together, the four groups represent a mix of animal welfare and human-focused causes.That mix reflects the gala’s broader identity. While the evening is centred on pets, it also draws on the performing arts community to raise money for causes that matter to its audience.A growing platform for animal welfareThe Fetch Pet Gala is still young, but its first two years have already produced more than $1.2 million in donations. The 2026 event showed that the format can bring together celebrity performances, corporate sponsorship and direct action on pet adoption.For Cyndi Lauper, Ariana DeBose, Darren Criss and Bernadette Peters, the gala was a chance to use their visibility for a cause that goes beyond the stage. For the dogs featured on the green carpet, it was a chance to be seen, photographed and potentially adopted.The event’s growing total suggests that the formula is working. A night of music and theatre, paired with real-world adoption support, has become a meaningful force for animal rescue in New York.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Meet Niayah Hicks, the 18-year-old Houston baker who started making desserts at seven and built a business with 250,000 social media followers and long queues at her pop-ups
articles.summary: Niayah Hicks, 18, began baking at the age of seven with her parents and grandparents and launched Starr Bakery at 12.
articles.body: Niayah Hicks, 18, began baking at the age of seven with her parents and grandparents and launched Starr Bakery at 12. The Houston business and pop-up now has more than 250,000 followers across social media, and viral videos have brought hundreds of customers to Houston Farmers Market to try her flavoured rolls. Everything is made at home with help from her small team, including her father, mother and grandparents. Hicks now goes through more than 300 rolls a day, and she hopes one day to sell her products in stores and open her own brick-and-mortar shop.How did Niayah Hicks build her Houston baking businessAccording to The Houston Chronicle, Hicks sold baked goods at Randle High School while balancing her studies and softball. Selling food during school hours was not always allowed, so she sold to students and teachers after school instead.According to the report, Hicks chose entrepreneurship after graduating because she did not plan to attend college. She said she never expected to go viral or attract so much customer attention, and that she had thought it would be much harder.What makes Niayah Hicks' bakery pop-ups so popularStarr Bakery has more than 250,000 followers across social media. Viral videos helped the business grow, and hundreds of customers now wait to try her treats. She is known for pop-ups at Houston Farmers Market, where she sells a variety of flavoured rolls.According to the report, the menu changes every week but always includes the original roll, the Biscoff cookie butter roll and the roasted caramel pecan roll, which is topped with homemade caramel drizzle. Strawberry crunch, s'mores and matcha rolls are also among the popular flavours. After the launch of her chocolate chip salted cookies, Hicks said the item will stay on the menu, and more offerings will follow.How does Niayah Hicks run Starr Bakery from homeThe bakery is not run from a large building or a spacious commercial kitchen. Everything is made at home with help from a small team: her father, Anthoney Hicks, her mother, Ronnada Hicks, and her grandparents. Anthoney Hicks, who has worked in finance for more than 20 years, manages the business side and teaches his daughter about taxes, goods, brand protection and the long-term picture.According to the report, Hicks has been selling out of desserts for the past year and now goes through more than 300 rolls a day. She hopes to sell her products in stores and eventually open her own brick-and-mortar location. She told the Chronicle, "I always wanted to inspire people with my baking," and said people do not need to go to college to succeed in a business.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: In 2022, former British Army serviceman Ian Ferguson began stockpiling food after the Ukraine war began; now, at 71, he has 600 cans in his shed to prepare for a 100-day lockdown or national emergency
articles.summary: A 71-year-old former British Army serviceman in the UK has spent up to £1,000 stockpiling food and essential supplies, preparing for the possibility of a
articles.body: A 71-year-old former British Army serviceman in the UK has spent up to £1,000 stockpiling food and essential supplies, preparing for the possibility of a 100-day lockdown or a major national emergency. Ian Ferguson, who lives in Weymouth, Dorset, has accumulated around 600 cans of food in his garden shed, including soups, stews, beans, curries, rice pudding and fruit. However, he has no plans to stop adding to his collection.According to SWNS, Ferguson began stockpiling in 2022, following the outbreak of the war in Ukraine. The father of two initially started buying a few extra cans during his weekly grocery shopping, but his collection gradually grew to 600 tins stored in 13 large delivery boxes.Ferguson believes six tins of food a day would be sufficient for him to survive for at least 100 days without having to visit a supermarket. However, he insists that his preparations are not just about his own survival. He believes communities must come together and share resources during emergencies.Why Ian Ferguson has stockpiled 600 cans of foodFerguson, who owns a taxi company in Weymouth, said he began thinking about emergency food supplies after considering how quickly society could be affected if shops ran out of essential items.Speaking to SWNS, he said, “There’s a phrase ‘nine meals between mankind and anarchy’.”That’s three days. Imagine you didn’t eat for three days.“These days everyone is so impatient and intolerant it would probably be three meals before anarchy.“You’ve got insurance on loads of things in case something bad happens, so what’s your insurance for having food in the house?”Because money won’t be any good when the supermarkets run out.”Explaining how his collection grew, Ferguson said, “I’d go shopping about once a week and by four, six, eight tins, whatever, and stick them in big ASDA delivery boxes in my shed. I’ve got 13 boxes full of food.“Originally I thought I’d get to 500, then I got to 600, but I don’t think I’m going to stop.“I’ve got stews, soups, beans, I’ve got some curries in a tin, rice pudding, fruit.”If you’re hungry it doesn’t matter. Peas, pudding, carrots, stuff like that. You could mix them up.”Wind-up radios, camping stoves and other emergency suppliesFood is not the only thing Ferguson has gathered. His emergency supplies also include wind-up radios, camping stoves, sleeping bags, water filtration tubes, an axe, a saw and other basic tools that could help him collect supplies from nearby woods.He is also not particularly concerned about expiry dates, which he believes people often worry about excessively. However, food safety guidance distinguishes between use-by dates, which relate to safety, and best-before dates, which generally relate to quality.Ferguson told SWNS, “People are obsessed with use by and sell by dates.”They then go buy cigarettes with pictures of cancer-full lungs. We’re very selective about what warnings we’re going to heed.“Obviously supermarkets want you to keep buying.”He also stressed that people with food allergies should ensure they have suitable supplies stored for themselves.Former British Army serviceman worries about cyber warfareHaving served in the British Army during the 1970s, Ferguson said he understands the potential impact of nuclear, chemical and biological warfare. However, he is increasingly concerned about the threat posed by digital warfare and cyberattacks targeting essential services.He pointed to the possibility of cyberattacks disrupting water companies, supermarkets and supply chains, arguing that modern society relies heavily on digital systems.“Once the shops are empty, every supply chain is basically digital. It’s not some bloke with a clipboard and a pen writing what you’ve got. When it goes down, nothing will happen. Everything will freeze,” he told SWNS.Ferguson also believes people should keep some physical cash available in case digital payment systems stop working.“I think we need to keep physical money to keep autonomy and flexibility in this system.“People used to want tangible money. When your battery is flat on your phone, if there’s no machine working, it means nothing to you.”Although he does not have solar panels at home, he believes alternative energy equipment could become useful during an emergency, particularly if more households invest in it.Ian Ferguson believes community support is key to survivalDespite his extensive preparations, Ferguson insists that surviving a crisis would require more than food and equipment. He believes neighbours and communities would need to share resources and support one another.“If you have a community you can share stuff and work out nice things. I’m not looking at being the whole thing, I’m looking at being an active member of a community,” he said.“Food isn’t the only answer. This whole thing isn’t about me sitting there watching people starve.“Someone who may have solar panels might still have heating. I’m 71, I’m not buying solar panels now.“I hope the kindness of humanity would come out.”Ferguson acknowledged that some people have questioned whether he will ever need to use his stockpile. However, he said he would rather have the supplies and not need them than face an emergency without food.“I’ll open up the tins and give it to the birds and get on with my life.“I might’ve wasted £1000 or £2000 on food but I’d rather do that then get into a difficult situation and look at that money and wish it was food in front of me.“I am hoping for the best and preparing for the worst. I’m more comfortable with that.”UK Government launches Be Ready campaign for emergenciesFerguson believes more people stockpile supplies than they openly admit, partly because they fear their provisions could make them targets for theft during a national emergency.In October, the UK Government launched its Be Ready campaign, encouraging households to prepare for situations in which everyday services could be disrupted. The initiative aims to help people become more self-sufficient during emergencies and reduce pressure on emergency services.However, Ferguson believes the government could do more to help households prepare, including providing basic emergency kits and clearer guidance on essential supplies.Speaking to SWNS, he said, “They should say we’re going to take the fat off generators; they could be doing a lot more.“Selling a kit of stuff to get people started. That would be something.”They’re all for people helping themselves but they’ve got an obligation to do a little bit.“We need the government to articulate a story so everyday people understand the risk.”You use AI every day. articles.title: Europe is rehearsing its next move in Ukraine, and Putin may not like what comes after the war
articles.summary: Europe is stepping up preparations for Ukraine's post-war security, with 2,800 troops from 11 countries set to take part in a major military exercise in
articles.body: Europe is stepping up preparations for Ukraine's post-war security, with 2,800 troops from 11 countries set to take part in a major military exercise in Poland to rehearse a potential deployment aimed at deterring future Russian aggression.The exercise comes as European nations step up efforts to build security guarantees for Kyiv and prevent Moscow from launching another offensive once hostilities end.According to a report by Defense News, the exercise, named KOALICJA 26.2, will be held from November 9 to 22 under the joint leadership of Britain and France. Troops from 11 countries will participate in the drills, which are designed to test how a multinational force could operate in support of Ukraine after a ceasefire.The exercise will involve land, air and maritime operations, including troop movements, logistical coordination, force protection and the integration of military command structures. Britain and France are leading the preparations, while Poland will play a key role in hosting the drills and facilitating military movements.The air component will involve British RAF Typhoon fighter jets and Voyager aerial refuelling aircraft, while Turkey will separately prepare for maritime operations, including mine-clearing activities in the Black Sea. The exercise will also test how participating countries can coordinate military resources and support operations across different domains.Ukraine's post-war security guaranteesFor Ukraine, the proposed deployment is part of a broader effort to secure long-term guarantees against another Russian invasion.President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has repeatedly stressed that any peace agreement must be backed by clear commitments from western allies on how they would respond if Moscow resumes its military offensive.In an interview, Zelenskyy said he wanted the arrangements to be clearly defined in writing. "If Russia starts (attacking) again, what will happen? Who will do what, with what means, and when?" he said, according to the Associated Press.The issue has also featured prominently in discussions among European leaders.At a January 6 meeting of the Coalition of the Willing in Paris, French President Emmanuel Macron, Then-British Prime Minister Keir Starmer and Zelenskyy backed a framework for security guarantees that would include a multinational force, continued military assistance and commitments to respond to any future Russian attack. Macron said the guarantees were essential to ensure that a peace agreement did not become "a new threat to Ukraine".The proposed multinational force would therefore form one part of a wider security arrangement rather than act as Ukraine's sole line of defence.The Ukrainian armed forces would remain central to deterring Russian aggression, with European allies committing to long-term weapons supplies, training, intelligence cooperation and military assistance. The force would be deployed only after a credible cessation of hostilities and at Kyiv's request.The proposed multinational deployment has faced strong opposition from Moscow, with Russian President Vladimir Putin repeatedly warning European countries against sending troops to Ukraine, even under a post-war security arrangement.In September 2026, Putin warned that deploying European military contingents, including peacekeeping forces, would risk triggering a direct confrontation with Russia. "This would mean war with Russia," he said, according to a report by The Washington Post.Moscow has maintained that the presence of foreign military contingents in Ukraine would pose a threat to Russian security. Following the January 2026 meeting of the Coalition of the Willing in Paris, Russia's foreign ministry warned that Western military units and infrastructure deployed in Ukraine would be treated as legitimate combat targets of the Russian armed forces.You use AI every day. articles.title: Eateries put South Fort walls at risk in Thiruvananthapur​am
articles.summary: Street food stalls near Thiruvananthapuram’s South Fort walls raise heritage damage concerns, with tents, wastewater discharge and congestion despite warnings.
articles.body: T’puram: The historic Fort walls in the capital are facing renewed neglect, with streetside eateries operating close to the heritage structure and causing potential damage after nightfall. The problem is worse at South Fort.Several makeshift food stalls have come up along the stretch, adjoining the fort walls, adjacent to the road to Enchakkal. Tents are pitched close to the structure, while wastewater from the eateries is reportedly discharged at the foot of the walls. The area remains crowded late into the night, with customers and vehicles adding to congestion around the heritage site.Residents said the stalls were being allowed to operate despite the area’s heritage significance. They alleged that the vendors showed little concern for the fort wall, with cooking, washing and waste disposal taking place close to the centuries-old structure.“People come here at night to eat, but no one seems to care about what is happening to the fort walls. Wastewater is being dumped at the base and the structure is being treated as if it were an ordinary roadside wall,” said a resident Subramanian B.Some of the stalls are set up by the side of the warning board fixed by the archaeology department.The West Fort gateway and the surrounding fort structures are part of the historic precinct that includes the Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple, palaces, and other monuments. The fort was built during the reign of Marthanda Varma in the 18th century.The 250-year-old West Fort gateway was recently repaired after its plaster had peeled off, exposing the brickwork. Nevertheless, traders and hawkers had set up shops too close to the fort wall.Earlier attempts by authorities to remove encroachments and roadside stalls have failed to produce a lasting solution.While a centralised food street has been proposed to regulate roadside vending, residents said immediate steps were needed to protect the West Fort walls.Subramanian alleged that the lack of regular monitoring and enforcement reflected the authorities’ indifference towards the heritage precinct of the city, which served as the capital of the erstwhile princely state of Travancore.Heritage enthusiasts have been raising the issue. But neither the corporation nor the department is able to prevent the hawkers, regulate traffic and protect the fort walls.Stay updated with the latest Thiruvananthapuram news. Download the TOI App.

articles.summary: Bihar health minister Nishant Kumar urges cancer awareness, timely screening, early detection and prompt treatment on National Cancer Awareness Day.

articles.title: Absconding Pocso accused held at Chennai airport while attempting to flee abroad
articles.summary: Pocso accused who absconded after trial in 2019 Kallambalam case was arrested at Chennai airport while attempting to flee abroad; lookout notice aided detention.
articles.body: T’puram: A 28-year-old man accused in a Pocso case, who allegedly absconded after the completion of the trial and before the court could pronounce its verdict, was arrested at Chennai airport while attempting to leave the country.The accused, Jain, a native of Kallambalam, was taken into custody on Thursday. He had been absconding after the trial in the case registered by Kallambalam Police in 2019 was completed before the Varkala Pocso court.According to the police, the case pertains to the alleged repeated sexual abuse of a nine-year-old boy between 2017 and 2019. The accused allegedly entered the child’s house on several occasions and subjected him to sexual abuse.The police said the accused disappeared after the completion of the court proceedings, at a stage when the verdict was yet to be pronounced. Following his failure to appear before the court, an arrest warrant was issued against him on Aug 29, 2026.The police subsequently intensified efforts to trace him and issued a lookout notice, alerting immigration and other authorities to prevent him from leaving the country.As the accused continued to remain absent, the court also issued notices to his sureties on Sept 14.The lookout alert eventually led to his detention at Chennai airport.The police said further legal procedures would be completed, and the accused would be produced before the court. The arrest comes after months of efforts to trace him following his disappearance before the pronouncement of the verdict in the case.Stay updated with the latest Thiruvananthapuram news. articles.title: CM unveils, announces projects worth over Rs 190cr in Keonjhar
articles.summary: Odisha CM Mohan Charan Majhi unveils and announces Rs 190 crore+ irrigation, health, education and sports projects in Keonjhar’s Raikala village.
articles.body: Keonjhar: Chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi on Saturday inaugurated, laid foundation stones for and announced a string of irrigation, healthcare, education and sports projects worth over Rs 190 crore during a visit to his native Raikala village in Keonjhar district.The major projects include three lift irrigation schemes worth around Rs 120 crore, the Rs 17.97-crore Jhumpura community health centre (CHC), a Rs 24-crore sports complex and a Rs 30-crore residential school for SC/ST students at Raikala. The CM also inaugurated a new State Bank of India branch in the village.The three lift irrigation projects at Raikala, Satikudar and Jarakani, covering parts of Keonjhar and Mayurbhanj districts, are targeted for completion by 2028. They are expected to provide irrigation facilities to 4,280 hectares of farmland, benefiting villages in Jhumpura and Keonjhar blocks as well as the Jarakani region of Mayurbhanj.Majhi said the govt plans to bring 15 lakh hectares under irrigation over the next five years. “When farmers thrive, Odisha thrives,” he said, adding that improved irrigation would enable farmers to grow two to three crops a year and help increase their incomes.The CM further said Rs 14,500 crore has been allocated for irrigation projects in the current budget.Underground pipeline systems are being developed under the Anandapur Barrage, Lower Suktel and Kusumi Barrage projects, he said.Majhi announced that the long-awaited Kanupur irrigation project in Keonjhar would be inaugurated in Dec.The CM also inaugurated the Jhumpura CHC.Besides, Majhi announced a Rs 24-crore sports complex at Raikala and a Rs 30-crore residential school for SC/ST students. He said 10 grassroots-level projects worth Rs 8.2 crore had been taken up in the area, including a mini stadium, additional school classrooms, development of Dhabaleswar temple premises, a rural market, Yuva Jyoti Club, renovation of Gramyashree Thakurani shrine and a kalyan mandap.The CM turned emotional while speaking about his native village. “Raikala is not only my birthplace, but a sacred place for me. Whatever position your son, your brother has reached today is only because of your blessings and the values of this soil,” he told a gathering, adding no matter how far one rises in life, one should never forget one’s roots. “I will never forget mine until my last breath,” said the CM.Referring to other projects in Keonjhar district, Majhi said Rs 313 crore was being spent on the development of Maa Tarini shrine, while a textile park was being developed for Rs 287 crore. A disaster recovery centre and data centre are also being established.Taking a swipe at the previous govt, Majhi said the earlier promise of providing irrigation to at least 35% of land in every block had remained “only on paper”.“This govt belongs to the poor, farmers and working people,” Majhi said, reiterating his govt’s commitment to the all-round development of Keonjhar.Keonjhar MP Ananta Nayak, Patna MLA Akhil Chandra Naik, Telkoi MLA and district planning board chairman Fakir Mohan Naik, and Keonjhar special development council chairperson Mamita Naik were among those present.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bhubaneswar | Silver Rate in Bhubaneswar | Bank Holidays in Bhubaneswar | Public Holidays in Bhubaneswar | Petrol Price in Bhubaneswar | Diesel Price in Bhubaneswar | CNG Price in Bhubaneswar | LPG Price in BhubaneswarStay updated with the latest Bhubaneswar news.
